intro: Session boundaries depend on inactivity between neighboring events. A long session can continue indefinitely while each next event arrives within the timeout.
task: Start a new session only when the sorted timestamp gap strictly exceeds a timeout.
requirements: Require nondecreasing integer timestamps and integer timeout >=0. Return lists of zero-based event indices. Start a new session only if the gap from the previous event is strictly greater than timeout; equality remains in the session. Empty input returns [].
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Integer inputs must be Python ints, excluding bool, within the task-specific bounds or -1e9..1e9 when no narrower bounds are stated.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Compare consecutive events rather than measuring from the first event in a session.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Keep equal timestamps together even when the timeout is zero.

explanation: Session boundaries depend on inactivity between neighboring events. A long session can continue indefinitely while each next event arrives within the timeout.
Returning indices preserves a link to original records even when timestamps repeat. Sorting is required from the caller so the function does not silently reorder observations.
